stories.headline: Apple Officially Approves Tiny Corp Driver Enabling Nvidia and AMD eGPUs on Apple Silicon Macs

key_facts.fact: Apple signed Tiny Corp's TinyGPU driver extension, enabling AMD and Nvidia eGPUs to work on Apple Silicon Macs over Thunderbolt/USB4 without disabling System Integrity Protection.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has signed a driver for AMD or Nvidia eGPUs connected to Apple Silicon but there are some big caveats, and it won't improve your graphics.

key_facts.fact: The driver is designed for AI research and LLM inference, not gaming or graphics acceleration. Video to an external monitor is not accelerated.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple approved drivers enabling AMD and Nvidia external GPUs to function on Mac systems. However, the software is specifically designed for AI applications rather than gaming purposes.

key_facts.fact: A Mac mini M4 with a Radeon RX 7900 XTX via Thunderbolt/USB4 achieved 18.5 tokens per second running Qwen 3.5 27B, a 27-billion-parameter language model.
key_facts.excerpt: A Mac mini with an M4 chip connected to a Radeon RX 7900 XTX via Thunderbolt/USB4 achieved 18.5 tokens per second running Qwen 3.5 27B.

key_facts.fact: Supported GPUs require AMD RDNA3+ or Nvidia Ampere+ at minimum, with macOS 12.1 or later and a Thunderbolt 3/USB4 port.
key_facts.excerpt: It requires a Mac running macOS 12.1 or later, a spare USB4 or Thunderbolt 3 port or newer, and a supported GPU with an enclosure that delivers sufficient power.

key_facts.fact: This marks the first time macOS has supported third-party discrete GPUs on Apple Silicon through an officially sanctioned mechanism, after more than a year of Tiny Corp engineering custom userspace GPU drivers.
key_facts.excerpt: After more than a year of engineering custom userspace GPU drivers, the approval marks the first time macOS has supported third-party discrete GPUs on Apple Silicon through an officially sanctioned mechanism.

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Completes First Manual Piloting of Orion Spacecraft in Deep Space

key_facts.fact: NASA astronaut Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen manually piloted the Orion spacecraft for 41 minutes starting at 9:09 p.m. EDT on Flight Day 4, testing six-degrees-of-freedom and three-degrees-of-freedom thruster modes.
key_facts.excerpt: Koch and Hansen took turns controlling the spacecraft starting at 9:09 p.m. EDT. For 41 minutes, the pair tested two different thruster modes, six degrees of freedom and three degrees of freedom.

key_facts.fact: At wakeup on Flight Day 4, Orion was approximately 169,000 miles from Earth with the Moon at 110,700 miles, as the crew prepared for the lunar flyby scheduled for April 6.
key_facts.excerpt: At wakeup on flight day 4, the spacecraft and its crew were approximately 169,000 miles from Earth and approaching the Moon at 110,700 miles.

key_facts.fact: The crew reviewed lunar surface features selected by NASA's science team for observation during their six-hour flyby, which begins at 2:45 p.m. on April 6 when cabin windows will point toward the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: After the piloting demonstration, the crew reviewed a list of the surface features the NASA science team had asked them to analyze and photograph during their six-hour flyby.

key_facts.fact: The crew captured the first-ever human-eye views of the Orientale basin, a 930 km multi-ringed impact crater on the Moon's far side that scientists use as an archetype for understanding impact basins across the solar system.
key_facts.excerpt: Artemis II shares new images as it gets closer to the moon.

key_facts.fact: Commander Reid Wiseman and Pilot Victor Glover will repeat the manual piloting demonstration on Flight Day 8 (April 9) to gather additional spacecraft performance data.
key_facts.excerpt: Wiseman and Glover will repeat the demonstration on Flight Day 8 (April 9).

stories.headline: US Rescues Downed F-15E Weapons Officer After 7-Hour Mission Deep Inside Iran

key_facts.fact: An F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over southern Iran on Friday April 3; the pilot was rescued within hours but the weapons systems officer (WSO), a colonel-rank airman, remained missing for 48 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: The F-15E jet carrying two members was flying over southern Iran when it was shot down on Friday morning local time. Although US forces rescued one crew member hours after the crash, the second pilot was yet to be found.

key_facts.fact: The WSO was rescued on Sunday April 5 by US Special Operations with Air Force Special Warfare attachments in a mission Trump called 'one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S History', lasting seven hours over Iran with heavy firefighting.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump called it 'one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S History' and confirmed the officer was 'seriously wounded' but 'will be just fine'. The mission lasted 'seven hours over Iran'.

key_facts.fact: The CIA launched a deception campaign inside Iran, spreading disinformation that US forces had already recovered the airman, to disrupt Iran's search efforts while using 'unique capabilities' to locate him.

'This was the ultimate needle in a haystack but in this case it was a brave American soul inside a mountain crevice, invisible but for CIA's capabilities.'

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC claimed its forces destroyed two C-130 aircraft, two Black Hawk helicopters, and an MQ-9 Reaper drone during the US rescue operation in southern Isfahan.
key_facts.excerpt: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed destruction of two C-130 aircraft and two Black Hawk helicopters during the rescue operation, plus an MQ-9 Reaper drone.

key_facts.fact: Iran had offered a reward of approximately $60,000 to anyone who located and turned in the missing WSO, in what appeared to be an effort to capture an American prisoner of war.

stories.headline: Planet Labs Indefinitely Withholds Iran Satellite Imagery at US Government Request

key_facts.fact: Planet Labs announced on April 5 it will indefinitely withhold satellite imagery of Iran and the Middle East conflict region, expanding a previous 14-day delay policy imposed last month.
key_facts.excerpt: Planet Labs will indefinitely withhold satellite imagery of Iran and the Middle East conflict region, expanding a previous 14-day delay imposed last month.

key_facts.fact: The restriction applies retroactively from March 9, 2026 and is expected to remain in effect until the conflict ends. Planet Labs stated: 'These are extraordinary circumstances.'
key_facts.excerpt: The blackout applies to imagery dating back to March 9, 2026. 'These are extraordinary circumstances, and we are doing all we can' to balance stakeholder needs.

key_facts.fact: The US government requested all satellite imagery providers voluntarily restrict access to imagery of designated areas of interest. The Pentagon declined to comment on intelligence matters.

stories.headline: Russia's VPN Crackdown Triggers Nationwide Banking Outage, Durov Links to Telegram Ban

key_facts.fact: Sberbank, VTB, and T-Bank all experienced service outages on April 3, affecting mobile banking, ATM withdrawals, payment transfers, and Russia's Fast Payment System. The Moscow Metro was forced to allow free entry.
key_facts.excerpt: Sberbank stated it 'restored all services' by noon after acknowledging that 'some' customers were experiencing difficulties. Services impacted included payment transfers, ATM cash withdrawals, mobile app access, and Russia's Fast Payment System.

key_facts.fact: Telegram founder Pavel Durov on April 4 blamed Russia's VPN crackdown for the outage, stating that 65 million Russians still use Telegram daily via VPNs despite the ban, and the government's VPN blocking broke banking infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Telegram was banned in Russia — yet 65M+ Russians still use it daily via VPNs. The government has spent years trying to ban VPNs too. Their blocking attempts just triggered a massive banking failure.

key_facts.fact: Roskomnadzor demanded Russian media remove reports linking the banking outage to government internet blocking measures, including articles from Forbes Russia and the Mash Telegram channel.
key_facts.excerpt: Roskomnadzor demanded that Russian media remove reports linking a major banking outage on April 3 to government internet blocking measures. Articles from Forbes and the Mash Telegram channel disappeared.

key_facts.fact: Moscow has intensified a crackdown on internet use and Telegram, pushing Russians to adopt a state-run 'super-app' called Max modeled after China's WeChat. Digital Development Minister Shadayev on March 30 said the government will 'reduce the use of VPNs'.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow has in recent months intensified a crackdown on internet use and applications it doesn't control, as it presses Russians to adopt a state-run 'super-app' called Max, modeled after China's WeChat.

stories.headline: Artemis II Enters Moon's Gravitational Sphere as Crew Prepares for Historic Flyby

key_facts.fact: Artemis II entered the Moon's sphere of influence on April 5 — the point where lunar gravity exerts more force on the Orion spacecraft than Earth's gravity — ahead of the first crewed lunar flyby since Apollo 17 in 1972.
key_facts.excerpt: Artemis II will reach the lunar sphere of influence on April 5, before flying around the far side of the Moon on April 6.

key_facts.fact: The lunar flyby is scheduled for Monday April 6 and will last up to five hours, during which the crew will photograph the lunar surface including areas of the far side never seen directly by humans.
key_facts.excerpt: The flyby will last as long as five hours, during which the crew will be mainly focused on taking pictures and videos of the moon, including areas of the far side of the Moon never seen directly by humans.

key_facts.fact: The crew — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen — launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center aboard SLS.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen launched on the Orion spacecraft on April 1, 2026.

key_facts.fact: On Flight Day 3 (April 4), the crew conducted spacesuit tests on Easter Sunday and prepared the cabin configuration for the lunar flyby approach.

stories.headline: March 2026 Confirmed as Hottest March in 48-Year US Satellite Temperature Record

key_facts.fact: Satellite data confirmed March 2026 as clearly the warmest March in the 48-year satellite temperature record for the contiguous US states, substantially exceeding the previous record set in 2012.
key_facts.excerpt: March 2026 was clearly the warmest in the 48-year satellite temperature record for the contiguous U.S. states. The previous record occurred in 2012.

key_facts.fact: The March heat wave set over 7,000 daily high-temperature records, nearly 2,000 monthly records, with 160+ cities recording their hottest March on record and 17 states setting new statewide March highs.
key_facts.excerpt: The heat wave set over 7,000 daily high-temperature records and nearly 2,000 monthly records, with over 160 cities experiencing their hottest March on record and 17 states setting new statewide March high-temperature records.

key_facts.fact: A new all-time US daily high temperature record for any March day of 112°F was set during the Southwest heat wave, which Yale Climate Connections ranked as one of the six most astonishing weather events of the century.
key_facts.excerpt: The 2026 heat wave set a new U.S. daily high temperature record for March of 112°F. Yale Climate Connections ranked it as one of the six most astonishing weather events of the century.

key_facts.fact: Despite record US warmth, the global satellite temperature anomaly for March was +0.38°C, and averaged over all Northern Hemisphere land areas March 2026 was 'uneventful, and was even cooler than 2024 and 2025'.
key_facts.excerpt: Global anomaly: +0.38°C for March 2026. Spencer notes that 'averaged over all land areas of the Northern Hemisphere, March 2026 was uneventful, and was even cooler than 2024 and 2025.'

key_facts.fact: Across South and Southeast Asia, up to two billion people have been affected by extreme heat, with temperatures running 7 to 12 degrees above normal in early 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Across South and Southeast Asia, up to two billion people have been affected by extreme heat, with temperatures running 7 to 12 degrees above normal.
